html:
The Dalabon, also called Dangbon, are an Aboriginal people of southwest Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, in stone country at the headwaters of rivers that run north and south.

Their neighbours include the Rembarrnga, the Jawoyn and the Kunwinjku peoples of western Arnhem Land. Their language is not part of the Pama-Nyungan family. Many Dalabon people later lived at Beswick, now called Wugularr, and Barunga, south of Arnhem Land. The language has very few speakers today. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Dalabon, also called Dangbon, are an Aboriginal people of southwest Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, in stone country at the headwaters of rivers that run north and south.
